stories.headline: Barcelona lift ban on supporters' group for Aston Villa clash
stories.summary: Barcelona has lifted a ban on different supporters' groups ahead of Tuesday's Champions League home game against Aston Villa following a positive meeting.
stories.body:
Barcelona has lifted a ban on different supporters' groups ahead of Tuesday's Champions League home game against Aston Villa following a positive meeting.

Barça had temporarily banned the operation of 'Gol 1957,' known as the "animation" stand, for Saturday's league match against Alavés after a member of that group struck Real Madrid player Eduardo Camavinga with a flag during the Clásico at the Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Barcelona executives met on Monday with representatives of those responsible for managing that section before announcing it would reopen that stand.

"The spokespersons have committed the groups to behave in a civic and respectful fashion in the stands," the club said.

"The club values the positive nature of the commitment undertaken by the supporters' group, which plays an important role in backing the team during the game. The club will monitor closely this commitment. Behaviour that led to the ban have brought repeated financial penalties and expose the Club to the possibility of having to close the stadium.

"FC Barcelona is confident that with everyone's commitment, this situation will not be repeated to the good of the members, fans and the club itself."

- Aston Villa's Pau Torres relishing chance to face Lamine Yamal

stories.headline: Liverpool's $500m forward line is failing. Can they turn it around?
stories.summary: Liverpool's star-studded, expensively assembled attack has scored fewer Premier League goals this season than Ipswich. That needs to improve immediately.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta described it as "remarkable." His Arsenal side had just beat Liverpool 1-0 to secure their first victory at Anfield in more than 14 years, but there was one element of the Premier League champions' performance that appeared to please their manager more than any other.

For the first time on record (since 2003-04), Liverpool had failed to record a shot on target at home in the Premier League, with Gunners goalkeeper David Raya enjoying a surprisingly uneventful afternoon on Merseyside.

"I didn't know about that statistic, but that's incredible," Arteta said in his postmatch news conference. "It didn't feel like this to be fair on the pitch because there were very little margins sometimes when they had the opportunity to shoot and it's a team that shoots a lot. You have to be so good at blocking shots and preventing those spaces for them to get into there.

"Again, it's a commitment of every single player in every action consistently to deliver those kind of stats and to do it against this team, it's something remarkable I would say."

- Arsenal get big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from

- Arteta, Alonso, Iraola: Three top managers all come from one tiny club

- Ex-Liverpool star Milner runs NYC Marathon in just over three hours

Arteta's assessment was fair. While Liverpool did not do enough to test Raya, they didnpose problems for the Arsenal defence. After falling behind to a Kai Havertz goal in the 16th minute, the hosts pinned the Gunners' back and played with an intensity reminiscent of Jürgen Klopp's "heavy-metal" Liverpool sides.

The Reds had 28 touches in their opponents' penalty area in the first half -- the most on record (since 2008-09) by any team in the opening period of a Premier League game against Arsenal -- and could have been awarded a penalty for Jurriën Timber's shirt pull on Alexander Isak inside the box. Florian Wirtz later hit the crossbar with a free-kick, while Alexis Mac Allister ought to have done better with a header he put over the bar.

However, the fact remains that Liverpool are still not consistently functioning as a fluid attacking unit. They have scored just four goals at Anfield in the Premier League this season, their joint-fewest after five home matches in a top-flight campaign (also four in 1913-14 and 2012-13). In three of their five home league games this term -- against Fulham, Manchester City and now Arsenal -- the Reds have failed to find the back of the net.

So why is their star-studded attack struggling to deliver? And how can manager Andoni Iraola get them back on track?

Big guns not firing
Going into Sunday's game, the matchup was pitched in some quarters as attack vs. defence. The absence of Bukayo Saka plus question marks over the fitness of Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis had left Arsenal looking shorn of quality up front, while Liverpool's forwards had appeared to be finding their feet during a run of five straight wins in all competitions.

Before the weekend, Isak had scored six goals in his last seven league appearances and had scored in three consecutive games for the first time in more than 18 months. Summer signing Bradley Barcola had registered five goal contributions in four games, while Wirtz had begun to look quietly impressive in the No.10 role.

After Liverpool spent a combined total of £354 million ($462 million) to sign that trio over the past three transfer windows, there was optimism that Liverpool's big guns were beginning to fire on all cylinders just in time to inflict some damage on the reigning champions. In reality, none of the three were able to produce a moment of magic against Arsenal. Adding in Cody Gakpo's £37 million ($49 million) signing in 2023, Liverpool first-choice attacking quartet cost them more than $500 million.

Not for the first time this season, Wirtz was substituted while his team were in need of a goal, ending the afternoon with an expected assists value of just 0.06. Barcola's influence waned after a promising spell in the first half, while Isak enjoyed just 26 touches and completed 12 of his 16 passes.

While Arsenal deserve credit for the robustness of their defence, Liverpool just aren't scoring, or even creating, enough chances in the Premier League. Having scored just 63 league goals under Arne Slot last term -- their lowest tally since 2015-16 -- there has not yet been a significant uptick in that department under Iraola.

Liverpool have scored 11 goals in nine top-flight games this season, two less than newly-promoted Ipswich Town and only one more than Michael Carrick's faltering Manchester United side. In terms of big chances created, the Reds are also performing poorly and currently rank 19th in the league with seven. Comparatively, the best-performing team by that metric, Manchester City, have created 32.

The concern for Iraola will be that Liverpool's stats are actually down from last season. After the same number of games in 2025-26, they had created 24 big chances (ranking second in the league behind City).

There has been a similar decline in other attacking metrics, with the Reds having completed 90 passes into the penalty area this term, down from the 115 they managed in nine games last season. The number of carries ending in the attacking penalty area has also dropped from 167 in 2025-26 to 137 in 2026-27.

Champions League form not translating domestically
It has been a different story in the UEFA Champions League, where Liverpool have scored 12 goals across their three games this season.

"I don't really know the reason," Iraola said last month when quizzed on why his side are more prolific in Europe. "It's true that the LASK game is different, but against Villarreal and Atlético Madrid, I think we've been offensively, especially, really good.

"In the Premier League, we are not scoring at this level and also we are probably defending better. They are different kind of games and different kind of opposition, I think more than [the difference being] the competitions, it is who you have played against."

Admittedly, Liverpool have had a favourable draw in the Champions League this term, but it's clear several of their players feel far more comfortable playing in European competition than they do domestically.

In a recent interview with French outlet Téléfoot, Barcola acknowledged that the Premier League is "less technical" than Ligue 1 and a big step up physically. It is no coincidence, then, that he and Wirtz in particular thrive when they are not having to contend with the intense physical demands of the English game.

Enduring issues in other areas of the pitch are not helping Liverpool up front. Iraola is still searching for the right balance in midfield and boldly handed teenager Trey Nyoni his first league start against Arsenal. After a few nervy moments and heavy tackles in the opening exchanges, the 19-year-old excelled as the Reds' deepest-lying midfielder, with his tally of 53 completed passes and 14 line-breaking passes the most of any player during his 59 minutes on the pitch. While his minutes will need to be managed as he adjusts to a more prominent role in the first-team squad, his development could prove vital in helping to better platform Liverpool's attackers.

There is also much for Iraola to ponder in terms of his full-backs. Milos Kerkez is full of endeavour, but his quality on the ball is a hindrance at times. On the other flank, the addition of Barcelona loanee Ronald Araújo has helped to shore up Liverpool's defence, but his natural instincts as a centre-back means he has limitations offensively.

Ultimately, this iteration of Liverpool is a work in progress. Sources told ESPN that Iraola's propensity for improving attacking players was one of the main reasons for his appointment, but he is just 14 games into his Anfield career and while some of the early signs have been promising, it will take time for him to fully realise his vision.

The 44-year-old coach will also hope that the expected return of France international Hugo Ekitike from an Achilles injury in the coming months can equip his squad with some additional firepower.

"Some days it feels like we are at the top, and some days it feels like we are not even close," midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai told Viaplay after Sunday's game. "It takes time to be at the top, I think."

It was an astute appraisal. Iraola's Liverpool are at the beginning of their journey. How quickly they reach their destination depends on whether his expensively assembled front line can begin delivering on their potential.

stories.headline: Luka scores 42 points, earns high praise from Giannis as hot streak continues
stories.summary: Luka Doncic's volcanic scoring spree continued Monday with 42 points in the Lakers' 138-117 win over the Heat, prompting Giannis Antetokounmpo to call him "one of the best scorers to play this game."
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Luka Doncic's volcanic scoring spree continued Monday with 42 points in the Los Angeles Lakers' 138-117 win over the Miami Heat.

Doncic's fourth 40-plus-point game in his past five outings raised his league-leading scoring average to 38.8 points per game.

And the performance prompted heady praise from Miami star Giannis Antetokounmpo -- who is averaging the fourth-most points this season but still nearly 10 fewer than Doncic (28.4).

"Obviously, he's one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best," Antetokounmpo said after L.A. improved to 6-2 with the win over the struggling Heat (2-5).

A reporter interrupted Antetokounmpo's answer, hoping for additional context for the two-time MVP's claim.

"Right now?"

"Not right now," Antetokounmpo replied. "Not right now. Of all time. I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he's got to be up there."

Coming from a guy with nearly 22,000 career points and positioned No. 41 on the all-time scoring list -- just a spot behind Larry Bird -- that's saying something.

But there are numbers that support Doncic's case, such as his career scoring average of 29.32 points being right behind only Michael Jordan (30.12) and Wilt Chamberlain (30.07).

Or how the win over Miami was Doncic's fifth straight game with 20-plus points in the first half, becoming the first Lakers player to do so since Kobe Bryant in 2007.

Or how the 27-year-old star is on pace to earn his second straight scoring title and third of his career.

Or how his career playoff scoring average of 30.9 points is even better than his regular-season mark.

"It just feels almost anything he shoots, whether it's a circus shot or regular step-back 3, or it's a tough floater, it just seems like everything he's shooting is going to go in," Doncic's teammate Quentin Grimes said. "... I don't think I've ever been on the court when everything somebody shoots, you think it's going in. So, kind of crazy little heater he's on for sure."

In Doncic's past five games, he has averaged 43.4 points while shooting 53.2% overall, 44.7% from 3 and 89.1% from the free throw line.

He added 13 assists Monday, handling Miami's double teams with ease: Doncic was blitzed when using an on-ball screen in seven possessions against the Heat, and the Lakers scored on six of those.

"It's a really good offense that we're playing right now," Lakers coach JJ Redick said, pointing out the Lakers' 39 assists were the most they've had since he took over as their coach in 2024-25. "And a lot of that, of course, is Doncic and what he's able to do and bend the defense. And his shotmaking creates a lot of problems and then he can make every pass."

Doncic had little to add about his personal play, instead focusing on the Lakers moving up to No. 4 in the Western Conference standings two weeks into the season by going 2-0 in back-to-back games against Miami and the Toronto Raptors.

"Obviously when we win, it feels way better," Doncic said. "But obviously, it feels good."

ESPN's Tim MacMahon and ESPN Research contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli is F1 champion. But why didn't he get his trophy in Mexico City?
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli is F1 world champion, but he won't get his trophy until December. Why does the sport still deny its champions their crowning moment?
stories.body:
There was one rather significant thing missing from Kimi Antonelli's world championship celebrations in Mexico City: the world championship trophy itself.

Despite becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history, the Italian will have to wait until Dec. 12 to get his hands on the prize he has spent his life chasing. That is because, unlike almost every other major sporting competition, F1 does not hand its championship trophy to the winner at the moment of victory. Instead, Antonelli will receive it while wearing a tuxedo, in a sterile hall, at the FIA's annual prize-giving gala dinner in Shanghai in December, six weeks after clinching the title.

It is one of F1's more peculiar traditions, denying the sport the sort of iconic sporting image synonymous with its biggest prizes. Think of the World Cup, the Super Bowl's Vince Lombardi Trophy or NHL's Stanley Cup, just to name three. The moment of triumph and the presentation of the trophy are inseparable. It doesn't have to be a conventional trophy, either. The Masters has turned the previous winner presenting the new winner a green blazer one of the most iconic images in all of sports.

F1's championship trophy, by contrast, seems almost an afterthought. Many fans would struggle to recognise it, which seems crazy for the series which is the pinnacle of motor racing.

It is a shame, too, because it is an impressive piece of silverware. Introduced in 1995, the trophy is made of sterling silver with gold detailing and features the signatures of Formula 1's world champions, stretching back to Giuseppe Farina in 1950.

So why wasn't it visible in Mexico City?

The answer lies in the divide between Formula 1 and its governing body, the FIA.

While F1, owned by Liberty Media, controls the commercial side of the championship, the FIA oversees its sporting and regulatory affairs. The world championship trophy falls under the FIA's jurisdiction -- Antonelli on Sunday officially became the FIA Formula 1 world champion - and its regulations stipulate that it must be presented at the governing body's annual gala.

Liberty Media has been keen to make more of the championship trophy. Sources have told ESPN discussions over a change this year did take place -- as they have for successive years now -- that the trophy be presented to Antonelli the moment he won it this year. However, as has also happened in previous seasons, it was agreed the FIA would stick with the convention of previous seasons and opt against doing anything radically different this time around.

- Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Verstappen wins Mexico City GP for Red Bull; Antonelli seals historic title

- Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

The FIA has long argued that presenting the trophy at its gala is important to the occasion's prestige. The event celebrates champions from across motorsport, including rallying, endurance racing and karting, with the presence of Formula 1's world champion regarded as an important attraction for the younger winners.

There is also a sporting justification, as race results can be challenged or altered after the chequered flag, potentially changing the outcome of a championship. The FIA prefers to wait until those matters are settled before handing over its biggest prize.

That argument has some merit, although less so when Antonelli has wrapped up the championship with four races still to run. It rather falls apart altogether when considering what happens at every grand prix as it is the exact opposite of the practice the FIA puts forward in that instance. Individual race trophies are handed out immediately after the finish, despite those results also being subject to protests, penalties and subsequent disqualifications. If a result changes, the trophies simply change hands.

Look no further than Sunday's race in Mexico City for an example. Antonelli was clutching his third-place Mexico City Grand Prix trophy in his hands at different points during his celebratory moments on the podium and the ceremony which followed. That despite the fact a post-race penalty or protest could have moved him down the order after the fact -- it wouldn't have stopped him being champion, but it would have meant he should not have been on the podium. And yet, he did not have the world championship trophy in his hand for that exact same reason.

There is little reason why the championship should be treated differently to an individual race, especially when the current practice stops the trophy becoming a prize that champions can share with fans in the celebratory moments.

It seems a missed opportunity for a sport which has spent the past decade transforming the way it presents itself to the world. F1 has embraced new audiences, new technology and new ways of celebrating its biggest moments, yet its most prestigious prize remains tied to an awards dinner.

Antonelli will undoubtedly enjoy getting his hands on the trophy in Shanghai. But the moment he became world champion, surrounded by his Mercedes team and thousands of celebrating fans in Mexico City, has already passed and it is a moment Formula 1 cannot recreate.

stories.headline: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons lead the Bears past the Seahawks 34-17
stories.summary: — Jeffery Simmons ran out of the tunnel for the first time since joining the Chicago Bears with a new uniform, orange sleeves and a wide smile as he welcomed the move that put right into contention...
stories.body:
SEATTLE -- — Jeffery Simmons ran out of the tunnel for the first time since joining the Chicago Bears with a new uniform, orange sleeves and a wide smile as he welcomed the move that put right into contention with important games on big stages.


Then he delivered exactly what the Bears needed.


Simmons had a sack in his Bears debut as part of a dominant defensive performance that helped lead Chicago to a 34-17 victory over the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night.


“When I attacked the field, I wasn’t worried about the trade,” Simmons said. “I wasn’t worried about all the outside noise. All I was worried about is play after play, just give the team everything I got.”


Acquired last week from Tennessee for a package that included two first-round picks, Simmons took little time to make a big impact on a defense that had lacked difference-makers.


He had a sack on the opening drive, added another tackle for loss and finished with six tackles, three pressures and a pass defensed with coach Ben Johnson describing his impact as “profound." Chicago held Seattle to 252 yards and one third-down conversion on 11 tries.


“He has me up off of the bench,” receiver Rome Odunze said. “Watching them third downs, watching the defense in general to see what he’s going to do next. He brings the energy to them. Obviously, his play-making ability ignites the defense, ignites the offense, ignites the team as a whole.”


Caleb Williams was extremely efficient for the Bears (6-2) against one of the NFL's stingiest defenses, committing no turnovers, taking just one sack and throwing for 247 yards while completing 71% of his passes.


Williams' play helped set up three short touchdown runs by D'Andre Swift and that proved to be more than enough against Sam Darnold and the Seahawks (4-4), thanks to the impact Simmons had on the defense.


“We knew it was going to be challenging and this was one of the more elaborate game plans in terms of what we were asking (Williams) to do as well,” Johnson said. “He stayed calm and collected throughout. I think that there are some times where it can get a little bit chaotic and yet he didn’t allow that to happen.”


The defending champion Seahawks lost for the third time in four games and are now looking up at the NFC playoff standings and can ill afford many more slip-ups.


The loss ended a 30-game streak for Seattle in the regular season and playoffs — the fourth longest for any team in the Super Bowl era — of not losing by more than four points.


“We got beat. No other way to sugar coat it,” coach Mike Macdonald said. “When you look at the things that it takes to win in our league, we didn't do those things and they did.”


Sam Darnold went 17 of 34 for 188 yards and two touchdowns for Seattle, but his interception in the fourth quarter set up Swift's third TD that made it 34-17 with 4:41 to play.


The Seahawks struggled once again to run the ball despite their trade last week for three-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and the return of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price from injures. Seattle ran for only 81 yards.


“We’ve got to improve very quickly in the run game,” guard Grey Zabel said. “Got to get back to running the ball, take the pressure off our quarterback and wide receivers and our play-caller. Got to be able to move the line of scrimmage.”


The Bears started off well against Seattle's stout defense by putting together a 17-play drive on the opening possession to take the lead when Williams threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden.


The Bears added two more field goals in the first half and built the lead to 20-9 in the third quarter with another efficient touchdown drive that ended with a 1-yard run by Swift.


The Seahawks were bottled up by Simmons and the Bears for almost the entire first half before Darnold connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a 43-yard pass with 30 seconds left in the second quarter.


Things looked bleak for Seattle when Jason Myers had a 33-yard field goal blocked in the opening minute of the fourth quarter.


But DeMarcus Lawrence forced a fumble by Colston Loveland on the next possession that set up Darnold's 7-yard touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp, and Seattle converted the 2-point conversion to make it 20-17.


The Bears answered with another TD drive and put the game away after Darnold's interception.


Caleb covers his cleats
Williams covered up the logo on his Caddix brand cleats after reportedly getting fined about $35,000 the past two weeks for displaying an unauthorized logo.


Williams wore all black shoes in the game with no logo displayed to avoid another run-in with the league.


“Just to just to calm things down, man,” he said. "It was a big week, and not here to create any BS toward the team. I want to keep that to a minimum from my side. Obviously, I get a lot of media, and so just trying to minimize that as much as possible.”


Injuries
Bears: DL Grady Jarrett (groin) and DL Kenatvius Street (knee) left the game with injuries.


Seahawks: DL Leonard Williams left in the second half with a stinger and didn't return.


Up next
Bears: Host Tampa Bay on Sunday night.


Seahawks: Host Arizona on Sunday,

stories.headline: Misiorowski, three other members of Brewers among MLB award finalists
stories.summary: Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski is among four members of the World Series champions who are finalists for baseball's biggest individual awards.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski is among four members of the World Series champions who are finalists for baseball's biggest individual awards.

Misiorowski, a heavy favorite to win the National League Cy Young Award, was one of the top three vote-getters in balloting for the prize by the Baseball Writers' Association of America at the conclusion of the regular season.

Finalists for all the major BBWAA awards were announced Monday night on MLB Network. Winners will be revealed next week.

Gold Glove second baseman Brice Turang is in the running for NL MVP, and Milwaukee skipper Pat Murphy could become the first to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards. Brewers closer Trevor Megill is a finalist for NL Relief Pitcher of the Year, a new category this year in both leagues.

The awards finalists:

AL MVP: Houston slugger Yordan Alvarez is the favorite to win. Third baseman Junior Caminero from the American League champion Tampa Bay Rays and shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. of the Kansas City Royals are the other finalists.

NL MVP: Gold Glove center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs is expected to win after batting .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, becoming the seventh member of the 40-40 club. Turang and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers are also finalists.

AL Cy Young: It's between Toronto right-hander Dylan Cease, Cleveland lefty Parker Messick and New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler. Messick's top-three finish as a rookie earns the Guardians an extra pick after the first round of the 2027 amateur draft.

NL Cy Young: Chris Sale of the Atlanta Braves and fellow left-hander Cristopher Sanchez from the Philadelphia Phillies join Misiorowski.

AL Rookie of the Year: Messick is also a candidate here, along with Detroit infielder Kevin McGonigle and Boston left-hander Payton Tolle.

NL Rookie of the Year: New York Mets right fielder Carson Benge is joined by Cincinnati Reds infielder Sal Stewart and St. Louis Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt.

AL Relief Pitcher of the Year: The contenders are Tampa Bay closer Bryan Baker, Cleveland closer Cade Smith and Toronto closer Louis Varland.

NL Relief Pitcher of the Year: The other candidates besides Megill are Philadelphia closer Jhoan Duran and San Diego closer Mason Miller.

AL Manager of the Year: Kevin Cash from the Rays, Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox and Will Venable from the Chicago White Sox are in the running.

NL Manager of the Year: Murphy's challengers are Philadelphia's Don Mattingly and Atlanta's Walt Weiss.

stories.headline: Valkyries, Lynx, Aces all seen as WNBA title favorites
stories.summary: The defending champion Valkyries are seen as favorites to win next year's WNBA title at one sportsbook, while the Lynx and Aces are favorites at others.
stories.body:
After coming into 2026 as 45-1 underdogs to win the WNBA Finals, the Golden State Valkyries captured their first title in just their second season in existence. Golden State's odds to do it again next season are much shorter, but sportsbooks around the country have not come to a consensus on who should be favored for the championship.

The Valkyries are the favorites to win the 2027 WNBA Finals at BetMGM, showing +300 odds, but at DraftKings, the Minnesota Lynx -- who notched the 2026 regular season's best record -- are the favorites at +310, while Caesars Sportsbook and FanDuel have the Las Vegas Aces favored at +340 and +360, respectively. The 2026 runner-up Atlanta Dream are within the top four at each of those sportsbooks, showing a short number of +400 at DraftKings.

Bookmakers have different rationales for where they placed each team on the Finals odds board. DraftKings director of sports operations Johnny Avello favored the Lynx despite their unceremonious end to the 2026 season and some offseason uncertainty.

"Minnesota's power rating is slightly above Las Vegas, Atlanta & Golden State," he told ESPN by email. "The pairing of last year's Rookie of the Year, Olivia Miles, and Napheesa Collier is lethal, as they are two MVP type players. Only concern is that Collier is a free agent, and could sign elsewhere. Atlanta is also marginally ahead of Golden State as they strengthen the team by getting Brionna Jones back, who played just nine games this past season."

Caesars Sportsbook's lead pro basketball oddsmaker, David Lieberman, noted that his book's power ratings are mostly the same from the end of the season and that "the championship odds mostly reflect the potential ceiling of each team" taking into account how things could shake out in the offseason.

Just outside the top tier are Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever (+900 at DraftKings) and Paige Bueckers' Dallas Wings, who are a relatively long 14-1 at DraftKings but as short as +750 at BetMGM. There's also a wide range of odds on the New York Liberty, who are anywhere between +900 and 17-1 for the 2027 title after a relatively disappointing 2026 campaign that saw them come in as favorites.

Indiana has perennially been one of the most popular futures plays by public bettors since Clark joined the league, but Dallas has been encroaching on that territory since Bueckers' debut. Both teams bowed out of the 2026 playoffs in the first round, and bookmakers aren't putting too much stock into their championship aspirations just yet especially given other teams' talent and some potential roster changes.

"The Fever need to re-sign Kelsey Mitchell, or their odds will go even higher," Avello said. "We're not worried about the general public piling on them to win it all -- their liability wasn't as high as the prior two seasons. New stars continue to emerge in the league, which does take some of the attention off Clark."

The Wings, meanwhile, "are a young and exciting team, but it remains to be seen if they'll be able to play enough defense to truly compete for a title just yet, similar to the questions surrounding the Fever," Lieberman said. "I expect to see quite a lot of action on both teams throughout the offseason in the futures markets."

Avello also said DraftKings is wary of the Washington Mystics, who were a surprising playoff team this season after coming into the 2026 campaign with 150-1 championship odds. Washington's young core has them at 35-1 for the 2027 title at DraftKings and as short as 11-1 at BetMGM.

For all of the potential contenders atop the board, there is also a cadre of long shots at the bottom, with the Chicago Sky, Seattle Storm, Toronto Tempo and relocating Houston Comets coming in at 120-1, per DraftKings lines.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

Dreyer -- a back-to-back MLS All-Star -- won't feature in this year's postseason, but that didn't stop him from handing the recently-crowded U.S. Open Cup champions a loss in a 1-0 victory over St. Louis. Dreyer's left-footed chip from distance was a taste of quality we'll be missing seven days from now.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 24

With no postseason hopes, victories must come from small achievements, like letting Reus assist three goals or having a goalkeeper make six saves while still conceding four.

26. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

Toronto succumbed to a 3-1 defeat to Atlanta and ended their postseason dream in the process. Back to the drawing board for Robin Fraser's side, who showed signs of potential earlier in the season.

27. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 28

With the playoffs out of the picture and the all-time goals conceded in a single season record newly secured, SKC still did their best to sabotage Dallas by absconding with a 1-1 draw against a side looking to lock up their top-two finish in the Western Conference.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Miguel Almirón won't appear in this year's playoffs, so he put on an end-of-season show in a 3-1 win against Toronto while eliminating the fellow Eastern Conference team from the playoffs. Five Stripes fans will take what they can get this year.

29. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

After losing to Toronto in the midweek, D.C. played Columbus with the playoffs already out of the picture and proceeded to lose 3-0. With 11 years since their last postseason victory, there's nowhere to go but up for this MLS original.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

It's too late to save their season, but not too late to sink somebody else's. A 91st-minute response to NYCFC's 1-0 lead secured their 26th point of the year and put to rest New York's postseason dream.

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: Man City relegated from Premier League but win Champions League? How it could play out
stories.summary: What would happen to Man City's superstar players if they get relegated from the Premier League but qualify for Champions League?
stories.body:
It has been over a month since the Premier League announced that Manchester City had been found guilty on 114 different charges of cheating the league's financial rules and obstructing the investigation into their potential cheating of the league's financial rules.

And ... we're still just sitting in limbo. Man City continue to play and win most of their matches, while none of us know what any of it really means.

They could be competing for another title. They could be wasting our time with meaningless matches that are about to get voided from the season. They could actually be in the middle of a relegation battle from a points deduction.

It's worth emphasizing: We're talking about the team that's currently in second place in the most popular league for the world's most popular sport -- and we don't know the stakes of any of the games they're playing! A speedy resolution -- or at least, a speedy resolution before the inevitable appeals process -- is necessary.

But until then, we're left to ponder the nature of reality in the wholly made-up structures of a made-up sport, and we're left to theorize about what might come next. So, theorize we will.

Given how harsh the language and the verdict were against City and -- how forceful City have been in their denials of their documented wrongdoing -- it seems likely at this point that the club will be relegated from the Premier League. Somehow, some way.

So, let's say that happens. You know what could also happen? Manchester City could win the Champions League.

Frankly, if they do get relegated from the Premier League via a massive points deduction or whatever other means soon, City might be even more likely to win the Champions League than they currently are. Sportsbooks, right now, have them as the sixth favorites -- after Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal, Bayern Munich, and Real Madrid -- with implied odds of about 10% to lift the European Cup.

So, then, let's say that both of those things happen: Manchester City get relegated from the Premier League, and Manchester City win the UEFA Champions League. If they did complete the dubious double, what would happen next?

How Manchester City could win the Champions League

I'm not so sure what Man City's relegation would look like in practice. But in a sense, it doesn't really matter.

I mean, it does matter. If City are given, say, a 100-point deduction or something, then the rest of the season means nothing to them. They'd still have to play games, but the stakes of those games would be no different than a situation in which the Premier League announced that City were no longer in the league and would play no more games for the rest of the season.

Both situations have all kinds of knock-on effects. If City are forced to play the rest of the season, then what about the teams that had to play City before they had nothing to play for? Is it fair for half of the league to get two games against a team that isn't trying and the other half to get only one?

But if the league just expels City and vacates all of their previous matches, then there's the problem of the lost attendance revenues for all of the Premier League teams that didn't get to play their home matches against City. That's probably an easier problem to solve but still a problem nonetheless.

However, in either scenario, we'd land here: Around 100% of Manchester City's focus would shift to the Champions League.

Maybe it wouldn't fully be 100% because they could still theoretically qualify for the Conference or Europa League through winning the Carabao or FA Cup if they're allowed to compete in those competitions. And qualifying for the Europa League while also getting relegated means they'd have an opportunity to bounce right back up into the Premier League and the Champions League if they then got promoted and won the 2027 Europa League, which they would be favorites to win -- even with the departure of a number of key players.

Those cups have so few games, though, that the point still stands: Almost all of Man City's energy would be put toward winning the Champions League.

Now, there are potential means for UEFA to attempt to expel City from their competitions, too, but given that City already had a UEFA ban overturned by an appeals court six years ago, I'm not sure how likely that would be. Remember: The Premier League's ruling of Man City's guilt applies only to the Premier League.

(You've probably heard some City supporters point to the 2020 victory over UEFA as proof of the club's innocence; it's not. They won the appeal because the court said most of violations were "time-barred," or too far in the past for UEFA to still enforce their punishment. They weren't exonerated of wrongdoing.)

So, if City are close to fully focused on the Champions League -- either because they're playing a bunch of academy kids and backups to see out the Premier League season, or because there are no other games to play -- then that would have to increase their chances of winning the Champions League, right?

We know that Premier League teams are, on average, adversely affected when they add the extra European matches to their schedule, so would not the inverse be true? Wouldn't the removal of Premier League games improve a team's performance in Europe?

The back-to-back titles of Paris Saint-Germain seem to suggest as much. Over the past two complete domestic seasons, the PSG outfield starter who has played the most league minutes is Vitinha, at 4,161. Among all outfield players across the Big Five leagues, that would rank ... 426th.

Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk led all players with 6,750 minutes played. Here's where some City players land: Antoine Semenyo was fourth with 6,398 minutes, Marc Guéhi was 14th with 6,209 minutes, Erling Haaland played about 5,700 minutes, and seven other City players featured more often than Vitinha.

While it's debatable how big of an advantage this is, there is one clear way it does provide an edge: Your best players are less likely to get hurt, so you're more likely to have your first-choice 11 featuring in the most important matches of the season.

Manchester City are still unlikely to win the Champions League (because no one is likely to win the Champions League this season), but this situation would have to make them more likely to win the Champions League. Based on the current odds, I'd feel comfortable saying that if City were relegated from the Premier League next week, they should move ahead of Real Madrid and become the fifth-most-likely team to win it all.

What if Man City got relegated and qualified for the Champions League?
The most similar situation we've seen to a potential City relegation was what happened to Juventus in 2006 after the Calciopoli match-fixing scandal.

Juventus had just won Serie A with 91 points -- 15 more than second-place Inter Milan. Per the Club Elo ratings, they were the third-best team in the world after Chelsea and Barcelona. At the time, they were also the third-richest club in the world after Real Madrid and Manchester United.

City are currently fourth in the Elo ratings, and they published the sixth-highest revenues in the most recently accounted for year. The club sits in pretty much the same chair that Juventus were kicked out of back in 2006.

After being relegated, Juventus lost the following players, priced at the following transfer fees:

• 24-year-old striker Zlatan Ibrahimovic: Inter Milan, €24.8 million

• 30-year-old midfielder Emerson: Real Madrid, €16.0 million

• 29-year-old fullback Gianluca Zambrotta: Barcelona, €14.0 million

• 30-year-old midfielder Patrick Vieira: Inter Milan, €9.5 million

• 27-year-old winger Adrian Mutu: Fiorentina, €8.0 million

• 32-year-old center back Fabio Cannavaro: Real Madrid, €7.0 million

• 34-year-old center back Lilian Thuram: Barcelona, €5.0 million

Yes, transfer fees were way lower back then. Also, yes, teams still hadn't really figured out how the age curve worked.

Essentially, Juventus had 10 players who started at least 20 Serie A games in 2005-06, and seven of them left the club after they were relegated. Juve lost both of their starting center backs along with one of the fullbacks, their two starting central midfielders, one of their starting forwards and a starting winger.

If we applied the same amount of turnover across the same positions to City, then it would look something like this: Rúben Dias, Marc Guéhi and Josko Gvardiol would all be gone. Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández? Bye-bye. Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland? Also out.

But the one big difference in the two situations would be if City did win the Champions League this season, and thus qualified for next season's Champions League.

If they did, then perhaps certain players could be persuaded to stay because they'd still get to compete in the top club competition, and they'd likely spend only one season in the second-division Championship. Even with all of that turnover, Juventus easily won Serie B with 85 points and a still-league-record 28 wins.

Plus, winning the Champions League would be worth around €170 million in revenue based on PSG's recent hauls. Except ... that's not close to making up what City would lose were they relegated down one division.

The broadcast revenue differential between the Premier League and the Championship would be closer to €300 million. Plus, the club would likely lose a ton of commercial revenue, presuming that all of their current commercial revenue is fair value, because (1) they'd be a toxic brand, and (2) they'd no longer be in the Premier League.

As my colleague Mark Ogden wrote about last month, it's hard to even imagine the mechanics of the fallout from City being relegated. They have the second-highest wage bill in the world after Real Madrid, per estimates from FBref. They wouldn't be able to afford anything close to that roster in the Championship, but Real Madrid and PSG are pretty much the only two clubs who could or would be willing to pay the same wages that City are currently paying.

Plus, you'd have to assume that most of the City players have some kind of clause in their current contracts regarding relegation because every current player signed their deal after the Premier League announced the 115 charges back in 2023. The players -- and their agents -- should have known this day was coming.

Based on FBref's estimates, if City moved on from those seven previously mentioned players, they would save around €130 million in wages. Combine that with the Champions League-winning revenue and you get close to making up the gap in lost broadcast revenue from dropping down a division.

But it gets more complicated for City. Not only would it be hard for those seven players to find new clubs that would pay them as much as they're currently getting paid, every other club in the world would know that City need to move on from these players.

City would have no leverage in negotiating transfer fees, especially because only a handful of clubs could afford the salaries of the players to begin with. Per Transfermarkt, the seven players Juventus moved on from had an estimated combined transfer value of €135 million at the time, but they moved for €84 million combined. That's a 60% discount.

We'd likely see something similar with City's dealings this summer -- or even this winter. And that, too, is a problem because of the strange way in which transfer fees are accounted for. Depending on how long the player has been at the club, City might have to take an accounting loss if the player moves on for a smaller fee than they paid to acquire him.

If City do win the Champions League this season and qualify for next season's tournament, it will make a difference. And it will make them even bigger villains than they are right now -- can you imagine anyone rooting for them as they run through the different rounds of the knockout stages? Depending on the draw, we could find ourselves in a situation where most of the world is rooting for ... Real Madrid and Jose Mourinho?

That would add just another strange emotional layer to what has been one of the strangest months in the modern history of European soccer. After years of spending pretty much whatever they wanted to acquire the best talent in the world, City will soon find themselves in a situation where they need all of the money they can get.

Winning their second Champions League would bring in a lot more cash over the next two seasons -- but it still won't be enough to change the fundamental reality: If Manchester City do get relegated, most of their most famous players won't be playing for Manchester City next season.
