stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli overcame George Russell, Ferrari to become F1's youngest champion
stories.summary: How Kimi Antonelli overcame early setbacks, teammate George Russell and a Ferrari fightback to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli was crowned the 2026 Formula 1 world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, sealing the title with four races of the season remaining.

He stood on the last step of the podium, behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in the Ferrari.

At 20 years old, Antonelli made his title fight look remarkably easy. He laid down the foundations with his maiden victory at the second race of the season in China, and with the exception of the occasional reliability setback with his Mercedes, he remained composed ever since.

It marked Mercedes' return to the top winning its first drivers' and constructors' trophy since Hamilton six years ago, and the team have well and truly unlocked their next superstar -- a superstar simply just enjoying himself.

Here are the highs -- and few low points -- that shaped his title-winning campaign.

- Kimi Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

- In pictures: The moments that defined Kimi Antonelli's F1 title-winning season

Melbourne crash, early favourite Russell wins opener
It was George Russell, not Antonelli, who was the name on everyone's lips coming into the season. Russell was one of the standout performers in 2025, while Antonelli's rookie season had been a rollercoaster. When it was clear Mercedes was the team to beat, Russell was the easy pick for the title.

By the time the season-opener had arrived in Melbourne, it was clear he had finally got what he dreamt of after a tedious four-year wait -- a fast and dominant Mercedes to match his ambition. It was an opportunity he couldn't afford to waste.

To anyone who had paid attention to 2025, it was perhaps not surprising how the opening weekend went. Antonelli showed flashes of pace but a crash in final practice left him on the back foot going into qualifying. TV cameras showed Toto Wolff and his race engineer Peter Bonnington comforting a disconsolate Antonelli after the smash.

Russell claimed pole, although Mercedes' quick repair job allowed Antonelli to get out and lock out the front row of the grid. The race was a showcase of F1's new era. F1's 2026 hybrid engine regulations featured a near 50/50 split between internal combustion and electrical power, but it was instantly met with driver criticism with Max Verstappen labelling them "anti-racing."

At the start of the race, Russell powered down to Turn 1 in a comfortable lead, but a sluggish start for Antonelli followed -- something that would be an early theme of his season. He quickly fought back through the order. A thrilling back and forth contest followed, as Ferrari briefly fought Mercedes for the win, but by the end it was as they were at the beginning -- Russell winning, although he had not been able to shake Antonelli, who finished just under three seconds behind.

Russell seemed overjoyed at the start.

"I love this car, I love this engine!" Russell declared over the radio after the race.

As for Antonelli, the young Italian had managed to avoid the disaster of his practice crash, but he was still tellingly hard on himself afterwards. To team boss Wolff, it was the kind of baptism by fire he expected the Italian would have in his sophomore season now the team was the benchmark car to beat.

"He's literally learning [F1] the hard way, which makes him stronger," Wolff commented on Antonelli after the race. "He was very, very strong on Friday and his pace on Saturday was there. But then the accident happened, and that can happen."

But anyone who thought the opening race of the season was a sign of things to come was gravely mistaken.

Championship standings after Australia:

Russell -- 25

Antonelli -- 18

China breakthrough changes everything
Mercedes showed the first glimpses of vulnerability in China with a series of front wing and technical problems, but it was not enough to stop another lockout of the front row. This time, Antonelli did not repeat any of his Melbourne mistakes, claiming a resounding first career pole position -- becoming the youngest driver in history to do so.

Antonelli had another sluggish getaway though, and after trying to cover Russell into Turn 1, the Mercedes drivers both allowed Hamilton's Ferrari to swoop into an early lead. Mercedes' strong pace quickly showed itself and Antonelli got back ahead a lap later, the beginning of a dominant and assured drive to his first win. It made him F1's second youngest winner of all time, behind Verstappen.

"I'm speechless," an emotional Antonelli said after the race. "I'm about to cry, to be honest. Thank you so much to my team, because they helped me to achieve this dream."

For anyone who had already handed Russell the title after Melbourne, Antonelli's Shanghai drive seemed to be a clear reminder the Brit would not have it all his own way.

It had been a monumental weekend for Antonelli with landmark pole and wins. A week later, he did the same again and took pole at the Japanese Grand Prix, with Russell nearly three-tenths behind. Again, Antonelli struggled at the start, dropping to sixth by the end of the first lap as Oscar Piastri and Charles Leclerc battled for the lead, with Russell fourth. The pendulum of the race seemed to be swinging back to Russell as he carved through the field, but a pit stop on lap 22 from the lead would prove his undoing. Almost immediately afterwards, Oliver Bearman crashed at Spoon, triggering a safety car.

It was manna from heaven for Antonelli, who effectively got a free pit stop, vaulting him up the order and ahead of Russell and Piastri.

"Unbelievable!" said Russell on his radio immediately afterwards.

Russell dropped to fourth by the end, a quite remarkable outcome for such a dominant car. Out in front, Antonelli surged clear, winning over Piastri by a dominant 17 seconds. Antonelli might have been fortuitous getting to the lead, but there was nothing lucky about the margin of victory: Antonelli was looking every bit worthy of his newest accolade and the youngest man to ever lead the world championship. Little did anyone know it then, but it was a lead he would never relinquish.

He would have several weeks to dwell on the new place in the history books, too, with the outbreak of war in Iran cancelling April's races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

Championship standings after Japan:

Antonelli -- 72

Russell -- 63

Three wins that broke Russell's challenge
The next three races underlined Antonelli's superiority and marked what would be the turning point in the season. Russell was no longer the established team leader waiting for the next generation to catch up -- Antonelli was in fact fully caught up. After the break caused by the Middle East cancellations -- Bahrain was subsequently moved to Malaysia in September -- Russell looked to fight back in Miami and the sprint appeared to suggest the title battle would swing back and forth. Antonelli out-qualified Russell comfortably but his Achilles heel from the year quickly re-emerged as he fluffed his start and dropped down the order. Norris and Piastri claimed a McLaren one-two while Russell was fourth and Antonelli sixth.

The momentum would swing again hours later. In qualifying again the difference between the pair was clear as Antonelli romped to his third straight pole position, with Russell languishing down in fifth. The young Italian's race start got the better of him once again and he ran wide at Turn 1 while Leclerc took a comfortable lead.

Antonelli and Leclerc fought out in front before Norris came into the mix and headed the field on lap 14. It was Antonelli vs. Norris for the rest of the race, before the Italian fended off the reigning world champion to take his third win in a row.

"This is just the beginning," Antonelli declared afterwards. "The road is still long, but we're working super hard and the team is doing an incredible job."

Canada followed and would deliver a blockbuster moment between the Mercedes duo. It was a Russell stronghold -- three pole positions to his name and a victory the year prior, the perfect place to kick life into his stuttering campaign. Russell started perfectly, taking a comfortable sprint pole, with Norris ahead of Antonelli in third. The mini-race featured a tense battle between the pair, with Antonelli being forced wide while trying a very ambitious move around the outside at Turn 1.

The Italian driver would then lose second after going wide a lap later while trying to pass Russell, losing second to Norris. Antonelli was fuming on the radio, leading to an intervention from Wolff. "Kimi, concentrate on the driving please, and not on the radio moaning," he said. Russell knew this weekend was his time to shine and he ended up stamping his authority and producing another stunning pole, but the race couldn't have gone any worse.

Both Mercedes drivers had a poor start while Norris took the lead before being called into the pits. Antonelli and Russell had fierce wheel-to-wheel battles for the best part of 27 laps, providing some excellent entertainment. Neither driver was willing to give an inch -- it seemed like all of Mercedes' worst nightmares coming back to life, with memories of Hamilton and Nico Rosberg's collisions in 2014 and 2016 while fighting each other for championships.

Fate would intervene before Russell and Antonelli were able to create another, with Russell retiring from the lead with a reliability issue while fending off his younger teammate. "It feels like the gods don't want me to be in this fight," a deflated Russell would say later. Antonelli's win rubbed salt into the wounds.

The Brit needed a clean weekend at the Monaco Grand Prix, but instead the problems continued. He qualified in sixth while Antonelli started on pole at a circuit where overtaking is notoriously difficult.

Monaco felt like a sucker punch to Russell. This time, Antonelli was flawless, taking a great pole. Antonelli's launch off the line was strong, but chaos unfolded behind him. In a race filled with incidents, Safety Cars and a red flag. Russell would be one of the drivers given a drive-through penalty for a minor pit-lane speeding infraction -- one later revealed to have been caused by the FIA incorrectly measuring pit entry. During a red flag, Russell argued his penalty should be deferred to after the race, but he served the drive-through anyway, dropping to the back.

Antonelli's win gave him another unanswered 25 points -- 50 in two races. While Canada had shown the raw side of Antonelli, Monaco had shown his class. Russell's championship hopes were slowly slipping from his grasp.

Championship standings after Monaco:

Antonelli -- 156

Russell -- 88

Ferrari fightback puts Antonelli under pressure
A team in red decided to join the title party and arrived to the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix with its first major upgrade -- and suddenly Mercedes had a title challenger.

Russell responded to his title struggles with pole, while Hamilton split the two Mercedes' to start the race second. A perfectly executed three-stop strategy played into the seven-time world champion's hands to make history and win his first race with the Scuderia, becoming the first driver of the season to end Mercedes' winning streak.

Antonelli suffered an electrical shutdown and was forced to retire from second place with just four laps remaining, while Russell gained some much-needed points in the title race. Hamilton cut the gap in the championship to Antonelli by 41 points -- making him a worthy title contender.

Antonelli lost 18 points in the championship and was downcast afterwards. He said: "I feel very empty emotionally right now, because we're trying to soak in what has just happened."

Russell arrived to Austria ready to fight back and locked out the front-row in what was a controversial pole position which occurred during a yellow flag period. He converted his pole into his second race win by nearly three-tenths from Antonelli, who stood on the final spot of the podium.

There might have been a glimpse of hope for Russell who said afterwards that he was "feeling like himself again." But that euphoric feeling was followed by a kick in the teeth at the next race when Antonelli bounced back at the British Grand Prix. He edged out Hamilton to win the sprint race after making a move on lap 8 of 17 from second. He crossed the line 2.7 seconds clear of Hamilton, with Norris third and Russell fourth.

The Italian took his form into the rest of the weekend with a stunning pole ahead of Leclerc. But during the race, it was the Ferrari man who had a mighty launch off the line to take the lead and win his first race in two years.

For Antonelli it was a race to forget as he scrambled for a point in ninth and desperately pleaded on the Mercedes team radio to stay out on track to seal a singular championship point. He was then demoted to 16th following a time penalty for exceeding track limits when he was struggling with car reliability.

It was a mixed bag of results for Mercedes, while Ferrari continued to build momentum. With the summer races in full swing, the championship fight was far from over.

Championship standings after Silverstone:

Antonelli -- 179

Russell -- 154

Hamilton -- 147

Antonelli strikes back

Russell's fightback did not last long. At Spa-Francorchamps, Antonelli got things back on track, claiming pole with a scintillating lap 0.3 seconds quicker than Norris in second, while Russell had to settle for fourth. The first lap seemed to be another of the micromoments which summed up Russell's year. Already starting down on Antonelli, Russell's electrical boost did not materialize in time for the Eau Rouge/Kemmel Straight on the opening lap.

Starved of power, Russell was swallowed up by other cars into Les Combes, tangling with Hamilton's Ferrari and ending in the gravel. "I'm out," Russell said on radio immediately after finishing. "What the f--- happened down the straight? I had no battery down the straight! Unacceptable! Unf------g acceptable!" If there was ever a radio message which summed up his mood and his season, Russell had delivered it. All of his hard work of the past handful of races, the gentle chipping away at Antonelli, was undone like that. Out in front, Antonelli briefly lost the lead to Verstappen, but soon got himself back in front to romp home to another comprehensive win.

Russell's engine issues would emerge again at the start of the Hungarian Grand Prix, as he struggled to get away and dropped from the third row of the grid to the back of the field. Out in front, McLaren's Norris capitalized on teammate Piastri's late race retirement to win.

Going into the summer break, Hamilton appeared to be just as big a threat to Antonelli's championship as Russell.

Championship standings after Belgium:

Antonelli -- 204

Hamilton -- 159

Russell -- 154

Forza Kimi!

Formula 1's summer break ended with the last Dutch Grand Prix to be held at Zandvoort under its current deal. Russell came into the second half of the season promising an all-or-nothing approach to his teammate's title lead and took sprint pole and then sprint victory to kick the season off in positive form.

The pendulum would swing back Antonelli's way the following day. Antonelli got the jump on Russell at the start before Verstappen crashed uncharacteristically on a wet-dry track. Antonelli briefly got ahead of Norris at the restart, but soon dropped behind the McLaren driver again. A late Virtual Safety Car gave Mercedes a dilemma. Antonelli pitted for fresh tyres to cover the threat of the looming Ferrari drivers, but rejoined behind Russell, who had stayed out on older tyres. Antonelli was quicker but also being caught by the two Ferraris. Mercedes immediately intervened, asking Russell to let Antonelli by into second position. Russell would oblige, despite a muted objection on the radio, and held off Hamilton to complete a double podium for Mercedes. It was odd to see a driver move over for a title rival, but showed how well Mercedes had managed the intra-team dynamic.

Rather than it becoming a controversy, Russell defended the call post-race. He said: "I mean, Kimi was ahead of me anyway. He deserved to finish ahead ... That's always just been our sort of rules, and the fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC [Virtual Safety Car], and he tried something different to, you know, protect us as a team."

The Mercedes call was a stark contrast to the Ferrari team, who at a key moment earlier in the race had dithered on asking Leclerc to move over to let Hamilton past, when the seven-time world champion was on a better strategy. Hamilton later argued it cost them a podium finish, at least. It suggested a team not all pulling in one direction -- and the tensions at F1's red team would explode into full public view one week later at Monza.

Antonelli's home Italian Grand Prix promised a moment of real jeopardy. Issues earlier in the season meant he needed a new engine and the back-of-the-grid penalty that came with it. Russell took a resounding pole position ahead of the two Ferrari drivers and it very much seemed game-on: yet another chance for Russell to try and change the momentum of the season, on Antonelli's home patch no less.

But Ferrari came into the race with bitterness lingering from Zandvoort. During qualifying at Monza, Hamilton -- the driver with the best mathematical shot at beating Antonelli -- had felt he was not given priority when it came to qualifying strategy. "The team was solely focused on trying to get an equal tow for each driver," Hamilton said, referring to the Monza trick of one driver giving his teammate an aerodynamic boost by doing a qualifying lap a certain distance ahead.

Hamilton continued: "We're at a point in the year where 59 points is a huge deficit to recover from, especially when Mercedes continue to be the leaders in speed. So yeah, we do have to work as a team. But have we been?" Hamilton then shrugged and shook his head, adding: "If and when that will ever change, we'll find out."

It seemed to be a clear plea from Hamilton for Ferrari to back him over Leclerc to try and wrestle the initiative back from Antonelli and Mercedes. Hamilton would get his answer in resounding fashion at Turn 1, when he got on the inside of Leclerc's car on the right-left first chicane. Leclerc refused to budge, pushing Hamilton wide and into the gravel. At the end of the second lap, Leclerc lost control of his car and crashed out. It was the most Ferrari of farces and appeared to end any chance the team had of making the rest of 2026 a two-team fight.

Antonelli's car, equipped with the new engine, was a rocketship. He was carving through the field, with each pass leading to a louder roar from the home crowd. He eventually caught Russell -- who had driven flawlessly out in front -- and, after one botched attempt at getting by which almost ended in the gravel -- Antonelli got ahead for a famous and emotional win, the first by an Italian at the Italian Grand Prix since 1966. Antonelli's 26 passes were the most recorded by a single driver at any race in F1 history. New engine or not, Antonelli had turned in the most magnificent of drives, dealt another bitter blow to Russell, and all while Ferrari fumbled a golden opportunity to give Mercedes some anxiety about a two-team fight. In a season of big moments, Monza was the moment.

As he stood on top of the podium, Antonelli soaked it all in. "The weekend itself was absolutely incredible," Antonelli said later. "Definitely so far the best day of my life, and an incredible memory. I couldn't wish for a better day." Two weeks later at Madrid's first-ever Spanish Grand Prix, Antonelli inched even closer to the title, as Norris' hopes of a win were undone by an awfully timed Safety Car. Antonelli would inherit the lead and keep Norris behind with a faultless drive under pressure to win Madring's processional debut event. Russell could only finish fifth.

Championship standings after Madrid:

Antonelli -- 292

Russell -- 211

Hamilton -- 191

Antonelli romps clear

Antonelli's perfect season appeared to hit a momentary roadblock in qualifying for Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where he dragged his front left tyre into the wall at Turn 1. It was a nightmare moment, a rare unforced error, as teammate Russell settled for second behind surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly. To anyone looking for a championship turnaround, there was historical precedent: Piastri's 2025 season had unraveled with unforced errors in Baku 12 months earlier. Was Antonelli about to trigger the same kind of implosion?

Out in front, Russell quickly got himself into the lead and controlled things from there, holding off old foe Verstappen over a tense final set of laps to record his first win since the Austrian Grand Prix. If Saturday had shown a glimpse of the raw side of the young Antonelli, Sunday showed why he was the champion-in-waiting, as he turned in a sensible and decisive drive to fifth, avoiding further drama on Baku's tight and twisty circuit. Russell's win felt important, but Antonelli had avoided a bigger points swing.

Verstappen's Baku performance had suggested a Red Bull resurgence and he confirmed it at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, a race which was as bizarre in name as it was in drama. A deluge before the start delayed the start, before F1's controversial new engines had a software glitch which caused a red flag before the end of the formation lap. When things finally restarted, Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen all traded places, before Verstappen took control of the race late on. As the finish neared, a final, decisive blow to Russell, as his Mercedes engine packed up a handful of laps from the end. Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first win of the year while Antonelli took an unanswered 18 points.

Russell's DNF was doubly costly, and it knocked him to the back of the grid in Singapore's Marina Bay street circuit. As had been the case a week earlier, Verstappen would control proceedings. Leclerc finished second, with Antonelli having a lonely race to third, but it saw him gain again -- Russell could only manage to fight back to ninth. The result meant Antonelli would go to Austin's United States Grand Prix with a slim mathematical chance of getting it done.

Championship standings after Singapore:

Antonelli -- 340

Russell -- 238

Hamilton -- 229

Antonelli gets it done in North America

If Monza a month earlier had been Antonelli's defining moment, Austin would feel like his unofficial coronation. He could claim the title if he won and Hamilton was fifth or lower and Russell was ninth or lower and arrived in Texas with a spring in his step. On Thursday, he seemed calm and relaxed and by Saturday he was in a perfect stride. Red Bull looked strong but Antonelli was on hand to deny them a pole position, delivering a beautiful lap late in Q3 to edge out Verstappen by 0.179 seconds. Hamilton and Russell settled for fifth and sixth on the grid, respectively, and suddenly the unlikely permutations felt a little less farfetched.

Race day came and it felt like Antonelli could get it done. But first he would have to navigate Verstappen -- the Red Bull opting to start on the grippier soft tyre off the line, while Antonelli and Mercedes opted for the medium, teasing a blockbuster run up COTA's hill to Turn 1. But anyone hoping for fireworks would be disappointed. Antonelli moved across to cover Verstappen at the start -- those sluggish getaways of the first part of the year a distant memory. The Italian immediately started building a lead as Verstappen was swallowed into a fight with the two Ferraris and Norris. Antonelli would only briefly surrender the lead in the pit stop phase of the race, but once back out in front he would disappear again, crossing the line 17 seconds clear of the next quickest car.

At one point, the maths made him champion, albeit briefly. Russell's race was hampered by a five-second time penalty, which turned an already poor event into a desperate one, and he soon dropped to ninth at the same point Hamilton was fifth -- exactly what Antonelli needed. By the finish, both had gained an additional place, meaning Hamilton finished fourth and Russell eighth.

Either way, it was a thumping win and felt like his championship affirmation moment. "Yes! That's how we f------ do it," Antonelli said on the radio after taking the chequered flag. "Let's do it."

Wolff felt like it was the standout drive of his young career. "For me, the best race that he's delivered so far," the Mercedes boss said. "Getting off the start with the inferior [medium] tyre and then controlling it at all times. The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional. So I think he's outperformed the car. Maybe it's a bit harsh to say, but I think his driving style just glues with the car."

It meant he needed just two points from the final five races to be champion and he would need to wait just seven days to start the party -- albeit after what he would describe as one of the most difficult weeks of his life.

Calm, jokey and mischievous in Austin, Antonelli arrived in Mexico City tense and unwell. He would miss Thursday's media session, later saying he felt "very bad." He added: "I had a high fever and stomach problems, so it hasn't been easy. But now I feel OK, just low on energy, just feel pretty tired, so it's going to be important to try and sleep well, because I haven't been sleeping well in these days, and hopefully tomorrow I will have more energy."

He clearly was not at 100% when qualifying came and, in a quirky twist on Austin, when his two competitors qualified down the order, they locked out the front row -- Hamilton claimed a spectacular first pole position for Ferrari, with Russell taking second place alongside his former teammate. Antonelli qualified fifth, which became fourth after a grid penalty for Verstappen. "I'm aware that definitely I haven't been driving well," Antonelli said afterwards. "I felt like already going to qualifying, I didn't feel great, and I felt a bit low on energy, so definitely, you know, it's not an excuse, but for sure, it hasn't been my finest performance."

The young Italian's plan to have a good night's sleep ahead of the biggest day of his life? "Bombard myself with melatonin," he said. Antonelli looked like a different man on Sunday, although he took a cautious approach to the start and standing restart that followed mid-race. There was drama ahead, with an clumsy Leclerc move on Hamilton handing Red Bull and Verstappen the win on a silver platter, but Antonelli didn't need to worry about any of it. A decisive move on Leclerc late on got him into the podium places and he spent the final laps of the race watching the two greatest drivers of his lifetime race for the win.

He admitted the view through his visor -- including that of Hamilton's Ferrari -- was getting blurrier as he neared the chequered flag. "[I was] already [crying] the lap before," Antonelli said later. "I think I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically. I couldn't see clearly ahead. You know, I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears."

Antonelli came home third, more than enough to clinch the title, to trigger wild celebrations with his team, and his family, who had flown in overnight from Italy to watch his crowning moment. "I am speechless, trying to process what just happened," Antonelli said later.

"A day I will remember forever. So grateful, thank you so much. I am going to enjoy every bit. I'm going to out with my family, friends and the team and we're just going to enjoy all the way because this is a very special moment and one we will remember forever."

The championship makes Antonelli F1's youngest, aged 20 years and 86 days.

stories.headline: Jeffery Simmons, Bears' defense handle Seahawks
stories.summary: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons had the Bears controlling both sides of the ball on MNF.
stories.body:
SEATTLE -- From the moment Jeffery Simmons stepped onto the field Monday night, his impact provided the Chicago Bears an immediate return on their investment after trading two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder for the All-Pro defensive tackle last week.

The move signaled the Bears are all-in on contending for a Super Bowl, and it paid off quickly as they took down the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17. It was their third straight win and fifth in their past six games.

Simmons elevated everyone around him on defense, and his impact was felt throughout. Seahawks QB Sam Darnold completed less than 50% of his passes with Simmons on the field and was a perfect 5-of-5 with a TD when he was off.

In consecutive games separated by 11 days, the Bears pulled off a franchise first, defeating the Super Bowl runner-up New England Patriots and then the defending champs in Seattle.

The Seahawks have lost three of their past four games.

Chicago Bears (6-2)

What to make of the quarterback performance: Right off the bat, Caleb Williams led the Bears on a 17-play, 80-yard touchdown drive, which was Chicago's longest opening drive since 2007 against the Packers. Williams used play-action passes, going 10-for-15 for 109 yards and a touchdown, the most completions and yards allowed by the Seahawks on play-action passes in a game this season. Seattle's defense entered Week 8 with the No. 1 pass defense in the NFL (144 yards allowed per game). Williams surpassed that mark by the two-minute warning in the first half and finished the game by completing 70.6% of his passes for 247 yards.

Most surprising performance: Credit the Simmons effect for injecting life into the Bears' ability to generate pressure with their defensive line in ways they couldn't the past two seasons, when they had a 25% pressure rate with a standard pass rush (four or fewer pass rushers). Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen didn't have to blitz as much as in previous games, and much of that can be credited to Simmons' presence. In 48 plays with Simmons on the field, the Seahawks' offense generated 146 yards (3.0 yards per play) and one touchdown to go along with three sacks and an interception. In eight plays with the All-Pro defensive tackle off the field, Seattle's offense had 106 yards and a touchdown and averaged 13.3 yards per play.

Stat to know: D'Andre Swift rushed 24 times for just 57 yards for a 2.4-yard average, but he ran for three touchdowns to boost his league-leading total to 10 (Buffalo's Josh Allen has nine). Swift is the first Bears player with 10 rushing TDs in a season since Raymont Harris had 10 in 1997. He is the first Bears player with 10 in the Bears' first eight games since Rick Casares had 11 in 1956.

Trend to watch: In back-to-back games, head-scratching blitzes at the end of the first half resulted in Chicago's defense giving up explosive, consequential gains. In Week 7 against the Patriots, the Bears rushed six instead of protecting the goal line with a 13-point lead and three seconds remaining, which led to a 48-yard TD. Up by 10 with 37 seconds left in the second quarter at Seattle, Chicago blitzed out of its dime defense on third-and-long and left cornerback Tyrique Stevenson isolated against Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Without any safety help, Stevenson gave up a 43-yard touchdown as the Bears clung to a 13-9 lead at halftime. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (8:20 p.m. ET, Nov. 8)

Seattle Seahawks (4-3)

The Seahawks made a massive addition to their offensive line last week by acquiring All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson in a trade. They got running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back from injury. But then they laid an egg offensively in their worst loss since December of 2024.

Much of it was due to quarterback Sam Darnold being under constant duress, likely a product of a reshuffled offensive line that was also missing left tackle Charles Cross (ankle). The offensive struggles gave the Seahawks no chance on a night when their vaunted defense looked as vulnerable as it has in a while, allowing season highs in points (34) and yards (363).

What to make of the QB performance: Make it six straight games with an interception for Darnold and nine total picks in that span. In his defense, his fourth-quarter interception was tipped right to a Bears defender. But he was far from sharp all night. Darnold was off target on 33% of his attempts in the first half, clearly affected by Chicago's pass rush. The Bears sacked him three times and registered six QB hits. Darnold finished 17-of-34 for 188 yards, two TDs and the interception. He had another would-be interception wiped out by a defensive holding penalty.

Stat to know: Before the Bears went 80 yards on 17 plays for a touchdown on their first possession, the Seahawks had not allowed an opening-drive TD since the 2025 opener. They didn't allow a score of any kind on the opening drive over the first seven games of this season. Seattle's defense -- which entered Week 8 allowing the second-fewest points in the NFL -- responded with a pair of three-and-outs against Chicago and forced a turnover in the fourth quarter that briefly gave the Seahawks life. But Mike Macdonald's unit -- which played without outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and lost defensive tackle Leonard Williams in the second half -- ultimately allowed too many chunk plays in the passing game.

Most surprising performance: The Seahawks entered Week 8 ranked third in ESPN Analytics' special teams rankings after finishing first in 2025. Yet that unit committed five costly errors. Rodney Thomas II botched an attempt to down a punt inside the 5-yard line, resulting in a touchback before the Bears' 80-yard touchdown drive to begin the game. Jason Myers missed a PAT and had a 33-yard field goal try blocked. Mike Morris was flagged for unnecessary roughness on a kickoff, giving Chicago an extra 15 yards on what would be a touchdown drive. Irv Charles was flagged for unnecessary roughness after a kickoff return, backing Seattle up before Darnold's interception. Even a good play by Jay Harbaugh's unit went for naught when Charles blocked a punt, only for the ball to bounce so far forward that it was as though it was never touched. -- Brady Henderson

Next game: vs. Arizona Cardinals (4:25 p.m. ET, Nov. 8)

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

With the World Series now behind us, players will be allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7-9.

However, as the current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, the 2027 season (as well as the financial rules that will govern it), players and teams alike may end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts do get signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) have received a qualifying offer from their current team and have until Nov. 17 to accept the deal or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club in order to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. stories.headline: Michael Jordan congratulates Valykries star Gabby Williams after WNBA title
stories.summary: His Airness had a simple message for the Golden State Valkyries star after her 30-point performance in Game 7.
stories.body:
OAKLAND, Calif. -- As Gabby Williams scrolled through the endless congratulatory text messages she has received since winning the 2026 WNBA championship with the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday night, one stood out from the rest.

It was from Michael Jordan.

"Stay hungry," the text read, Williams told ESPN on Monday.

She responded quickly: "I've never been hungrier."

Williams, who was crowned WNBA Finals MVP, scored 30 points in the first Game 7 in WNBA history while wearing a pair of Air Jordan 41 sneakers. Twenty-eight of those points came in the second half. Williams also added a game-high four blocks plus two steals.

The Chase Center and Bay Area are no strangers to incredible playoff performances. Some of those responsible for the memorable local area moments, including San Francisco Giants legend Barry Bonds and Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green, were courtside to see Williams'. As Valkyries owner Joe Lacob tells it, even they were amazed.

"Her second half ... legendary," Lacob said after the championship. "That was unbelievable stuff."

Her teammates felt the same.

"We've talked about it all season: We have Gabby Williams, and you don't," Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes said at exit interviews Monday. "[It] was one of the greatest things I've ever seen.

"She took it upon herself to make sure we weren't going to lose that game."

Golden State guard Veronica Burton said it felt like she was in the stands with the Ballhalla crowd watching Williams, even though she was on the court with her.

"You talk about being in the zone, and you hear about flow state, maybe you watch it on TV, but to be there in real time and to witness it was amazing," Burton said.

Williams, though, said she hasn't reflected on her Game 7 heroics. She's just sleepy.

"I'm just living in the moment," Williams said. "This was a really long month, a really long series. I've been focusing on my friends and my family, my loved ones and soaking this in with my teammates.

"Unfortunately, I don't think we'll ever have this exact group again. So I am trying to soak in this moment as long as I can with these people."

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 46
Goals: 41
Assists: 19

Nov. 1: New England Revolution 1-2 Inter Miami

Messi once again provided the magic touch for Miami, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Herons' marquee star set up a goal and scored the winner as Miami leapfrogged New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

After going behind to a Dániel Gazdag goal, Miami responded with a strike from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- before the 39-year-old scored the winner in the 83rd minute. Sumptuous stuff.

Oct. 28: FC Cincinnati 2-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists for Messi in what was an eventful 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

Luis Suárez scored in the 61st minute to give Miami a 1-0 lead, and then the reigning MLS Cup champions needed some late-game heroics to salvage a point. They still fell to third in the Eastern Conference, after New England beat Red Bull New York 3-2 on Wednesday.

Oct. 24: Red Bull New York 2-0 Inter Miami
It has been an eventful few days for Messi. Just a day before the match, he traveled to Spain to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first individual soccer player to earn the honor.

He then returned to the United States and joined his teammates in New Jersey, starting on the bench before coming on in the 56th minute. However, he was unable to make an impact as the hosts secured a 2-0 victory, ending Miami's three-game winning streak.

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: AFL 2027 fixture: Five must-watch games in the first month
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month.
stories.body:
The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month of action.

Get the popcorn ready and get set to enjoy these absolute belters in the new year.

5. Port Adelaide vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 4, Adelaide Oval, Sunday, April 8, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Make no mistake, when Zak Butters returns to Adelaide Oval to face his old mob for the first time since departing, it's going to be incredibly spicy.

In a move that shocked absolutely nobody, Butters left Port Adelaide during the 2026 trade period, inking a long-term deal with the Western Bulldogs. It's a brutal blow for the Power, and his ex-teammates will be sure to give him a hard time when they share the field in Round 4. You just know it's going to be on for young and old!

The AFL also made the move to schedule this blockbuster game as the closer to next year's Gather Round. It means far more bodies will be in Adelaide that weekend and a greater number of eyeballs on the clash.

4. Hawthorn vs. Geelong - Round 2, MCG, Monday, March 29, 3:15pm (AEDT)
The traditional Easter Monday clash between the Hawks and Cats is always on our shortlist of early season must-watch games, and next year will be no exception.

Both of these clubs are in the premiership window. Both clubs have added high-profile players this offseason. Both clubs have fanbases that bring an electric energy to Easter Monday at the MCG.

This one is also set to be a fascinating coaching battle between Chris Scott and Sam Mitchell, two of the game's best tacticians, who will go head-to-head just as much as the players on the field.

3. Fremantle vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 1, Optus Stadium, Thursday, March 18, 8:10pm (AEDT)
This Round 1 game in the west is simply oozing with intrigue.

Of course, the question on everyone's mind is how the Dockers back up after having this year's premiership ripped away from them in harrowing circumstances. Does it galvanise the club? Will we see 'Wharfie Time'? Surely not!

For the Bulldogs, they landed the biggest fish of the off-season in superstar midfielder Zak Butters. This will be the first opportunity to watch him play in his new colours, lining up in the middle alongside skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards.

2. Brisbane vs. Collingwood - Round 2, Gabba, Thursday, March 25, 7:50pm (AEDT)
Reigning premier Brisbane will unfurl its latest flag in Round 2 when it hosts Collingwood in its first home game of the season, a clash that has blockbuster written all over it.

The Lions are looking to become just the second team ever to win four consecutive flags (joining, you guessed it, Collingwood from 1927 to 1930) but will be doing it without superstar midfielder Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow medallist departed for the Magpies this offseason, making this early season contest between the two clubs extra intriguing.

Plus, any opportunity to watch current Brownlow medallist Nick Daicos play footy is reason in itself to tune in!

1. Hawthorn vs. Brisbane - Round 1, MCG, Friday, March 19, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Thankfully we don't have to wait long for the Hawks and Lions -- quite possibly the competition's two best teams -- to square off in 2027. And if this game delivers even 70% of what these sides dished up in this year's epic preliminary final, then we're in for an absolute treat!

Many have labelled Brisbane's thrilling win over Hawthorn this past September as the greatest game of footy played this century. That in itself should be enough of a reason for their next clash to simply be must-watch.

There will be extra intrigue with both teams given this clash falls in Round 1. For the Lions, they will be looking to navigate life without both superstar midfielder Lachie Neale and master coach Chris Fagan, while the Hawks will be attempting to integrate recruits Zach Merrett and Ben King into their line-up.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Dolphins win race for Sebastian Su'a
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news on Bradman Best's future and which clubs might be lining up a play for Sam Walker.
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Dolphins win race for Su'a

The Dolphins have won the race to retain Sebastian Su'a, with ESPN understanding the young forward has agreed to terms on a two-year extension that will keep him in Redcliffe until the end of 2029.

Several NRL clubs had identified Su'a as a potential recruitment target, but the Dolphins have moved to secure his future with the club.

Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension

Sua Fa'alogo has agreed to extend his stay at the Melbourne Storm through to the end of 2032, ESPN understands.

The agreement will keep the fullback in Melbourne for the next six seasons, securing a key figure in the Storm's long-term plans.

Fa'alogo's retention delivers a major boost for Melbourne ahead of the November 1 contracting window, with the club moving to lock down one of its most exciting talents.

Dolphins close in on Lemuelu extension, confident of keeping Farnworth

The Dolphins are closing in on a multi-year extension for Connelly Lemuelu as they also express confidence in retaining Herbie Farnworth.

ESPN understands Lemuelu is nearing an agreement to extend his stay despite interest from Canberra, Parramatta and Cronulla.

Securing the back-rower would deliver a retention boost for the Dolphins, with the length of the proposed deal yet to be confirmed.

The club is also understood to be confident it can retain Farnworth despite links to the Sydney Roosters.

While that confidence is yet to translate into a confirmed extension, keeping the English international alongside Lemuelu would help preserve key combinations on the Dolphins' left edge.

Eels edge ahead in Best race
Parramatta have emerged as the frontrunners to land Bradman Best, with multiple sources indicating the Newcastle centre is increasingly likely to join the Eels beyond 2027.

Best has been identified as a priority target for Parramatta, who are looking to bolster Jason Ryles' backline with an established representative star.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the Eels are understood to be in the box seat despite Newcastle's efforts to retain him with a lucrative extension.

Bulldogs unlikely to enter Walker race
Canterbury are unlikely to enter the race for Sam Walker, with the Bulldogs backing their existing halfback options ahead of the upcoming season.

Despite suggestions the club could emerge as a potential destination for Walker, it is understood Canterbury are taking a wait-and-see approach rather than preparing to launch a pursuit.

The Bulldogs' immediate focus remains on the internal battle for the No.7 jersey, with Mitch and Alex Conti set to compete for the role over the offseason.

Canterbury have not completely shut the door on a move should circumstances change, but their current position suggests they are unlikely to become an active contender for Walker's signature.

For now, the Bulldogs are content to watch how the situation unfolds.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid tracking Arsenal's Calafiori
stories.summary: Real Madrid are monitoring Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori as a primary target to strengthen their left back position. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori is on the radar of Real Madrid, while Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich are exploring a January move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are monitoring Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori as a primary target to strengthen their left back position, according to TEAMtalk. Los Blancos have already made initial inquiries ahead of a potential summer 2027 move, though any approach would require a substantial transfer fee to convince the Gunners to let him go.

- Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich are exploring a January move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi, reports The Mirror. The Cherries are reluctant to part ways with the 20-year-old mid-season, while Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is also eyeing Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz as he seeks attacking reinforcements.

- Manchester United scouted Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy during Der Klassiker against Bayern Munich, TEAMtalk reports. The 30-year-old scored his eighth goal of the season in the 2-2 draw, with United also keeping tabs on his Dortmund teammates Jobe Bellingham, Felix Nmecha and Daniel Svensson.

- Barcelona are eyeing Estoril defender Jordan Arnolin alongside Brighton & Hove Albion, according to Record. The 18-year-old Portuguese youth international has attracted attention from top clubs due to his defensive versatility and ability to operate in midfield.

- Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton is widely expected to leave Selhurst Park next summer, Football Insider reports. Despite the Eagles resisting interest in the previous window, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United continue to track the 22-year-old as he approaches the final two years of his contract. But a deal is expected to cost around £80 million.

Other rumors
- Barcelona have no plans to let midfielder Gavi leave, with head coach Hansi Flick viewing the 22-year-old as an important part of his long-term plans despite his limited starts this season. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Liverpool are looking to open contract extension talks with 35-year-old defender Virgil van Dijk before his deal expires next June. (TEAMtalk)

- Chelsea and Manchester United hold interest in Como defender Jacobo Ramón, though Real Madrid have a clause in his contract which allows them bring him back to the Bernabéu. (Football Insider)

- Paris Saint-Germain could challenge Manchester United for the signature of Atlético Madrid midfielder Pablo Barrios. (TEAMtalk)

- Benfica have entered the race to sign Boca Juniors defender Lautaro Di Lollo. (La Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Manchester United are pushing to secure the signing of VfB Stuttgart goalkeeper Dennis Seimen. (Ekrem Konur)

- RB Leipzig could consider letting winger Johan Bakayoko leave in January for an offer worth €12 million. (Philipp Hinze)

- Lazio are closing in on a new contract extension for winger Gustav Isaksen through the summer of 2031. (Nicolò Schira)

- Atlético Madrid have initiated moves to sign Almería midfielder Stefan Džodić. (Marca)
